title: After: the same model with the night-5 exact stack
subtitle: Same weights, same outputs: the n-gram table goes through the OS page cache, Qwen's draft head guesses ahead, and the CPU is now the only real wait

nodes.label: Router
nodes.desc: Unchanged: the same experts are picked, so the output is the model's own.

nodes.label: Draft head
nodes.desc: Guesses the next 2 tokens; the full model checks all 3 in one pass. 86% of guesses accepted.
nodes.notes: Database view: speculative execution. Checking 3 tokens costs about one token's expert reads, because consecutive tokens reuse most experts.

nodes.label: CPU
nodes.desc: Still computes 24 layers' experts: 31.88 ms of every 49.4 ms token. This is now the bottleneck.
nodes.notes: Next lever: move this work to a GPU (your profile + an engine that overlaps CPU and GPU), or add an eGPU. See the leverage table.

nodes.label: RAM page cache
nodes.desc: 99.97% of the expert pages the CPU needs are already here: decode no longer waits on the SSD.

nodes.label: Read pool
nodes.desc: Fetches next layer's likely experts ahead (his idea, our learned table). Measured: no gain here, because nothing misses RAM any more. It pays on SSD-bound boxes (the Mac, bigger models).

nodes.label: N-gram table
nodes.desc: Mapped like any other weight and read in at load (-lzm off). Bit-exact. Low page faults (~10 per token) in 8 of 8 runs; stock lazy mode was erratic (high faults in 7 of 11 runs).
nodes.notes: Database view: let the OS buffer cache handle an index lookup instead of a hand-rolled random reader.

flows.name: Generating (after)
flows.desc: Decode: 20.26 tok/s without drafting, 27.56 with, in the same server.

steps.note: The last token goes in; the router picks the same 10 experts per layer as before.
Its n-gram rows come from the OS page cache, read in at load.
Qwen's draft head guesses the next two tokens.
The GPUs run their 24 layers for all 3 tokens at once.
The CPU runs the other 24 layers for the 3 tokens; it reads about as much as for one.
Practically every expert is already in RAM: no SSD waits.
The CPU's 31.88 ms is now most of the token: that is what to attack next.

flows.name: Reading your prompt (after)
flows.desc: Prefill: ~110-170 tok/s in every -lzm off run (stock: 17-175 depending on the run).

steps.note: A prompt arrives in 512-token batches, as before.
8,000+ n-gram rows per batch come from cached pages.
The CPU-tier experts still stream to a GPU once per batch: the next limit for long prompts.
